To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
increased cerebrovascular pinocytosis and permeability to HPR is associated with early hypertension and that fibrin deposition is associated with late hypertension in SHR.

1) enhanced pinocytotic activity was associated with increased cerebrovascular leakage to HRP, 2) increased pinocytotic activities were associated with increased pinocytosis in cerebral arterioles, and 3) enhanced pinocytic activity was associated with medial hyperplasia and fibrin deposition in renal arterioles.

cerebrovascular permeabilty to HRP was increased in spontaneously hypertensive (SHR) rats, associated with enhanced cerebral arteriolar pinocytosis and with medial hypertrophy of the cerebral, ocular and renal arterioles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of cerebrovascular changes associated with hypertension.
the mechanisms of cerebrovascular damage associated with acute and chronic hypertension.
the study of the cerebrovascular permeation barrier in hypertension.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SHR strain used is not a good model of cerebrovascular disease, but the results obtained may be relevant to other models of hypertension and other cerebrovascular diseases.
the cerebrovascular changes were associated with enhanced pinocrptosis, and that the cerebral vascular changes were associated with increased pinocytosis and fibrinoid deposition.
the cerebrovascular changes observed in SHR are not due to a primary defect in the cerebrovascular bed but rather are secondary to systemic hypertension.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SHR strain studied is a good animal model for the study of the early changes in the cerebrovascular system.
the cerebrovascular changes observed in SHR are not due to the hypertension per se but to a genetic predisposition of this strain to cerebrovascular changes.
in SHR, the cerebrovascular permeable state is associated with a marked increase in the number of pinocyctic vesicles and is a manifestation of early cerebrovasular changes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cerebrovascular changes occur early in the SHR model and that enhanced pinocytic activity may be the primary cause of increased permeability.
